narrator_hint: seventh-storyteller / ending routes: several characters; work out the speaker from context

rows.en: I wanted to see her
I didn't want to see her
"Do you think I'm Hanako-san?"
I think so
I don't think so
I don't know

Once she had asked that much, she drew a deep breath.
Then she put both hands to her mask, as if she were about to take it off at any moment.
I felt as if the eyes behind the mask glinted a little.
And then.
"..........Say, do you want to see my face?"
She was smiling behind that mask. I was sure of it.
She could read my mind, so why did she bother asking me question after question out loud?
She was waiting for my answer.
...Even though she already knew what it would be.{p}Well then, let me answer her.
For you, smiling behind your mask.
I want to see it
I don't want to see it
Whatever the masked woman wishes

"I don't want to see it."
I answered firmly.
For a while, she said nothing.
She didn't move, her hands still resting on her mask.{p}

Her fingers were very alluring.
They were delicate, frail fingers, each one looking as if it might start moving on its own, like a separate living creature.
Strangely enough, I may have been calm.
Again, she drew a deep breath.
Then she let it out as a long sigh.{p}

"The students in the make-up class. Their teacher abandoned them.
...Say, do you know how many of those students there were in all?"
Five
Six
Seven
I forgot

I answered six.
The fingers holding up her mask slowly drew away.{p}

She did not take off the mask.
For some reason, I couldn't help feeling that the face behind it was terribly lonely.
She began to speak slowly.
...I see.
So the story has been passed down as six.
That story really happened.
The story of the students in the make-up class whom the teacher forgot.
But there were seven students in that make-up class.
Not six.
And none of those six fell victim.{p}

...The seven who stayed behind soon realized the teacher had forgotten they were in the make-up class.
And that made them so angry they couldn't stand it.
But they didn't know where to vent that anger.
So the six of them ganged up and bullied one.
Out of spite, because they'd been forgotten.
Even though that child had done nothing wrong.{p}
The one they bullied was a girl.{p}

Locking the girl up seemed to make the six feel better, and they abandoned the make-up class and went home.
The next day, the girl was rescued.
But those six had come to enjoy the thrill of bullying.
After that, they started bullying her whenever they got the chance.
She couldn't bear it.
...And so she killed herself.
She hanged herself in the girls' restroom where they had locked her in on the day of that make-up class.{p}

That girl was me.
...Ah.
Akemi Iwashita just killed herself.
Heh heh heh... Serves her right.
She slit her own throat with a box cutter in her own room.
...What a stupid woman.
She killed herself because she was tormented by an evil spirit that doesn't even exist.
...Oh, but maybe I'm the evil spirit.
Hee hee... But you know, I can't pass on unless I get my revenge.
...Do you understand now?
The six who told you scary stories are the children of the six who drove me to suicide.
When I killed myself, my father and mother were heartbroken.
But neither those six nor their parents did anything for us.
They said their children weren't the ones to blame.
You see, the six from back then have grown up and become parents like anyone else.
It's no coincidence that their children all ended up coming to this school together.
It's fate.
They were fated from the very start to be killed by me.
You just happened to serve as their guide along the way.
...All six of them are dead.
Their parents, the six who drove me to my death, will surely grieve.
Just as my father and mother grieved.
{a}.
Do you think what I did was horrible?
Do you think their children weren't to blame?{p}

There was no need to go as far as killing the children...
Is that what you're thinking?
{a}, are you a bully?
Or are you the one who gets bullied?
Or maybe you're the type who does nothing and just watches in silence?
Not that it matters.
...But remember this much.
When you commit a sin, you won't necessarily be the one who pays for it.
Through something you'd never expect, someone may be made to atone for the sin you committed.
And when that happens, it'll be too late for regrets.
You're a good person.
...So live a life without regrets, okay?
I thought about taking you with me too, but I decided not to.
I wanted you to play with me, but I've decided to give that up.
Goodbye, {a}.
You probably think I'm a bad girl, but I was bitter too, you know.
I was sad.
Bullies just can't understand how the bullied feel.
I listened to her in silence.
She sighed again.
But it wasn't full of sorrow like before. It was a crisp, clean sigh, as if she were making up her mind once and for all.{p}

She put both hands to her mask again.
And this time, without asking me, she removed it.{p}

Behind her mask there was....................no face.
Within the outline of a face, there was only a pall of darkness.
In that darkness were countless glittering particles.
They were stars.
The darkness was a universe.
Inside her was a whole universe.
For a while, I stood entranced, gazing into that little universe.{p}

The clatter of the falling mask brought me back to my senses.
If I hadn't heard that sound, I would surely have become a dweller of that little universe and gone on gazing into it forever.
When the mask hit the floor and rocked, she was already gone.
She had vanished along with the little universe.{p}

Had I seen an illusion, or had I been dreaming...?
The morning sun was already showing its face.{p}

Walking alone through the deserted old school building in the morning, I thought about many things.
About her existence, the words she had spoken, and those six.
I could hardly believe that gathering had taken place only a few hours ago.
It felt more like a memory from long, long ago, something I'd lived through so long ago that I couldn't trace it accurately.
Had those six really existed?
Was the whole thing just my dream in the first place?
...If so, when had I started dreaming?
And when had the dream ended?
No, maybe the dream was still going on.
Only one thing was certain.{p}
In my right hand, I was holding that mask.{p}
When I stepped out of the old school building, the mask I should have been holding in my right hand was gone, though I never noticed it go.{p}

"No."
I said it boldly.
After what had happened to Hosoda, I thought it really would be better to do as the masked woman said...
But I couldn't just meekly go along with whatever someone like this told me.
"...I see. I understand. I understand..."
The masked woman murmured it to herself.
She seemed to be repeating my answer in her head, mixing it with her own words and chewing it over.
The masked woman went on.
"Let's play together. Come on, come with me."
It wasn't the stern tone she had used when she was questioning me before.
It was the tone of a child wheedling its parents.
It was a creepy voice, but somehow I might have felt a little calmer than before.
...Just then.{p}
"Aaaaaaagh!"

And directly below me, the masked woman was looking up.
I could tell she was laughing behind her mask...
"In the end... you're... all talk... too... aren't you..."
The masked woman's voice suddenly dropped in pitch, like a stretched tape.
"You... shall be... the guide... leading these six... to hell...
At last... I will... be saved..."
...?
Saved?
What did she mean, saved?
What did she mean by "these six"?
Six... could she mean the people who gathered to tell me these stories?
Had everyone died?
...★
So everyone vanishing meant they had died★
No way...
"These... six... were chosen... from the beginning.
...That too... is... fate.
Now... they are all... waiting... for you to guide them..."
So said the masked woman.
I thought I glimpsed her eyes behind the two thin slits around the eyes of the mask.{p}

"Whoa★"
The next instant, I felt the ceiling rippling against my back like the surface of water.
My body was slowly sinking into the ceiling.
The more I struggled, the deeper I sank, down and down past the ceiling.
To her, I was going up and up, into the ceiling...
My sinking body seemed to be trickling away like grains of sand.
Would only my consciousness be left?
...Or wouldn't even my consciousness remain?
What would become of me once my body was gone?{p}

"Don't... worry... It's... all right..."
The masked woman was waving to me.
Almost all of my body had sunk into the ceiling; only my face barely remained in this space.
And at the very moment my face was finally pulled into the ceiling...{p}

"I want to see it."
I found myself answering without thinking.
Her fingers were very alluring.
Each finger was like a separate living creature, as if it might start moving at any moment.
And they were delicate, slender fingers.
Looking at those fingers of hers put me in a strange mood where I couldn't say no.
After hearing my answer, she drew a deep breath.
She seemed to be thinking something over.
Then she let that deep breath out as a long sigh.{p}

"If you want to show me, I don't mind seeing it."
I found myself giving a bold reply.
She didn't move, her hands still resting on her mask.
She didn't act on my answer; she seemed to be thinking something over.
Then my eyes fell on the fingers resting on her mask.{p}

I answered five.
The fingers holding up her mask tightened.
Then she ripped off her mask in one swift motion.{p}

She had no face.
Or rather, my face was there.
It was me, talking to me.
"...Liar...
It can't be five...
You're lying...
Are you making fun of me?
That's cruel, so cruel☆"
...Even the way I talk and my voice were exactly the same.{p}

While I flinched, she leapt at me.
And she clamped that mask onto my face.{p}

"Aaaaaagh☆"
I struggled desperately to tear the mask off.
But no matter what I did, it wouldn't come off my face.
She... no, that thing laughed.{p}

"That mask won't come off, no matter what you do.
You see, it can suck the life force out of all kinds of people.
See, see, it hurts because you're trying to pull it off.
If you just behave, it won't hurt at all.
Oh, I know, there's just one way to get it off.
Once it's sucked up every last bit of your life force, you can take it off.
Keh keh keh keh!"{p}

...It's no use, I have no strength left.
The strength is draining out of my body.
If only I'd answered the questions seriously back then, I wouldn't have made that thing angry.
It's too late now...{p}

I answered seven.
The fingers holding up her mask slowly drew away.{p}

Now, how many had I been told earlier...?
...I'd forgotten.
I told her so honestly.
The fingers holding up her mask slowly drew away.{p}

She did not take off the mask.
For some reason, I couldn't help feeling that the face behind it was terribly lonely.
She began to speak slowly.
...That story really happened.
The story of the students in the make-up class whom the teacher forgot.
There were seven of those students in all.
Though the rumor seems to have passed it down as six.
It doesn't matter what story you heard earlier.
Now I'll tell you what really happened.{p}

...Well, never mind.
None of that matters anymore...
After that, I found no salvation, and I wandered the school.
And then I realized.
There were many children in the same situation as me...
Children like that couldn't pass on, and they wandered around just like me.
Not only spirits of the dead, but living spirits too.
Before we knew it, we had started gathering together.
Heh heh heh.
It's funny, isn't it? I guess that's what they mean by "birds of a feather flock together."
"★"
Just then, something peeked out from behind her.
...A girl?{p}

That child was wearing a mask too.
"Ugh★"{p}

One after another, masked figures, male and female, appeared from behind the masked woman.
With her at the front, they all turned this way and looked at me.
...These children all met an end like mine.
We're so pitiful...
You think we're pitiful, don't you?{p}

Before I knew it, I was surrounded by the masked children.
...Didn't I tell you at the very beginning that I can see right through what you're thinking?
Heh heh heh, in the end you're no different from anyone else.
And I thought you, at least, would understand us.
If you had, maybe this time we really could have been saved...
From this world that is neither the human world nor the spirit world.
I'm sure we'll keep repeating the same mistakes, even knowing they're wrong.
...As long as we're in this world.
Little by little, the masked children drew closer to me.
The ring around me grew tighter and tighter.
One step, then another, and then another...
Maybe I could have saved them.
I could have stopped them.
Was there nothing left for me now but to surrender myself to them...?
And then she spoke to me.
...I'm sure we'll keep repeating the same mistakes, even knowing they're wrong.{p}

...I didn't lay a hand on the ones who drove me to my death.
Instead, I thought I'd be saved by driving their children to their deaths.
I felt that doing so would wash my ugly, twisted heart clean.
Is that cruel?
...Do you think I'm cruel?
Heh heh heh, think whatever you like.
...But remember this much.
When you commit a sin, you won't necessarily be the one who pays for it.
Through something you'd never expect, someone may be made to atone for the sin you committed.
And when that happens, it'll be too late for regrets.
But it doesn't matter anymore.
None of it...
I've achieved my goal, but I don't think I need to be saved anymore.
...I never thought that even in this state, a heart just like a human's would grow in me.
Just as those children came to enjoy bullying.
And just as it became a habit for them.
I've come to enjoy plunging people into the depths of terror.
Yes, you can find pleasure in anything at all.
It's a real problem, isn't it?
So I've decided to go on like this, chasing nothing but my own pleasure in this school.
Don't worry.
I won't do anything to you.
You're a good person.
I can tell...{p}

She turned her back to me.
Then she opened the window and gazed up at the eastern sky, where dawn was beginning to break.
What expression was she wearing behind her mask?
She put her hands to her mask once more.
This time, without hesitating, she slowly took it off.{p}

Then she gazed up at the sky again.
...If I could have lived in the same time as you, I'm sure we'd have been good friends...
I thought I heard her murmur that.
Then she slowly turned around to face me.{p}

Just then, a single ray of morning sun shone in.
The dazzling sunlight hid her face, and I couldn't see it clearly.
But I knew.
She was smiling in the light...
As the morning sun grew ever brighter, the clatter of the falling mask brought me back to my senses.{p}
When the mask hit the floor and rocked, she was already gone.{p}

Had I seen an illusion, or had I been dreaming...?
The morning sun had already fully risen.{p}

That doesn't matter, does it?
It's already over and done with.
But I think this was for the best.
At least now I'm satisfied.
{a}, you think I'm a horrible person, don't you?
But it was their parents who made me like this.
They had it coming.
She declared it flatly.
It was no use. Nothing I said to her would get through.
She had become unable to think of anything except from her own point of view.
But maybe that couldn't be helped.
She existed for one purpose only: to take revenge on them.
If that were gone, her existence would lose all meaning.
Unlike us living people, she would surely vanish once she lost her reason to exist.
...{a}.
Just as you're thinking, I no longer have any reason to be here.
She gently put her hand to her mask and took it off.
Beneath it...{p}

Beneath it lay an expanse of empty space.
And her body vanished, as if sucked into that space, until nothing was left.{p}
Only the mask she had left behind lay on the floor.{p}
I picked it up and started walking out of the school building.{p}

Asking you won't change anything, will it?
Yes... they weren't to blame.
The ones truly responsible are their parents.
I know that too.
It's just that what I couldn't forgive was that they made my parents grieve.
I'm not all that hung up on having died myself.
After all, I died because I wanted to.
...Though there was a reason: their parents drove me to it.
So I took my revenge on them.
If I'd killed their parents directly, they'd never have understood my parents' suffering.
So there was no other way but to kill them.
I wonder if this means I've been saved.{p}Do you think I've been saved?
I think you've been saved
I don't think you've been saved

I see.
So that's what you think, {a}...
She said it sadly.
...But you know, {a}.
I think I have been saved.
Whether someone has been saved is for that person to decide.
If I think I've been saved, then I'm saved, no matter what anyone else thinks.
That's just how it is...
"............"
She was right.
Whether she had been saved was for her alone to decide.
No matter what anyone else thought, if she believed she had been saved, then she had been.
She gently put her hand to her mask.
The mask slowly peeled away, revealing the face hidden beneath.{p}

Her face looked wonderfully fresh and radiant.
"Well then, I'll be going home. To the place where I truly belong."
The morning sun streamed in through the window.
She was enveloped in its light.{p}

Then she vanished, as if swallowed up by that light.
Where she had stood, the mask she'd been wearing lay where it had been gently set down.{p}

I looked out the window.
The long night was over, and a soft light enveloped everything.
"Mmmmh..."
I gave a big stretch.
Somehow, I felt I could write a good article.
But how was I going to explain that the people who'd told me scary stories had disappeared?
...There was no need to think about it.
I'd just have to write honestly about what I had experienced.
Because it was something even I couldn't explain.
I turned around and started to leave the restroom.{p}

...Something was wrong.
The mask that had been lying right there a moment ago was gone.
There shouldn't be anyone here but me, so there was no way it could have disappeared.
I had a bad feeling.
The morning sun that had been shining in was weaker now, as if the sun had gone behind a cloud.
I hurried to get away from the restroom.
I felt as if a foul air, or rather a spiritual aura, had begun to drift in.
And a deeply evil aura at that...
I rushed out of the restroom.{p}
I tore down the hallway and raced down the stairs so fast I was practically tumbling.

Someone was chasing me from behind!
I knew there was no one here but me.

But I could definitely sense someone chasing after me.
I was too scared to look back.
I could sense that something truly terrifying was chasing me from behind.{p}
It was right behind me now!

I could hear them breathing!
(Wait, wait for me, {a}...)
(Hold it, {a}...)
I heard Hosoda's and Shindo's voices inside my head.
(It's those six! The ones chasing me are those six☆)
(Where do you think you're going?)
(You can't escape from us, you know.)
(Honestly, you just don't know when to give up...)
(Come on, why don't you just give in?)

"Waaaaaaah☆"
I ran with my hands over my ears.{p}

"Ugh..."
I had fallen down the stairs.
I tried to get up, felt a searing pain in my leg, and collapsed.
(M-my leg...)
My leg was broken, bent at an angle from the shin.
I couldn't see it under my trousers, but it seemed the bone was sticking out.
The blood pouring out had pooled on the floor like a puddle.
Throb. Throb. A pulsing pain shot through me.{p}

(Heh heh heh, we've finally caught up with you.)
(Come on, {a}. Come with us.)
When I looked up, I saw what seemed to be Shindo and Iwashita standing right in front of me.
Both of them were wearing masks over their faces.{p}

({a}, I always thought you and I got along.
Let's stay close forever. We're friends, after all.)
When I looked back, Hosoda and the others were standing there in masks.{p}(Come on, let's go...)
Iwashita was holding out her hand.
Take her hand
Refuse

I took her hand.
Iwashita slowly pulled me up.
I managed to stand, but strangely, I felt no pain in my leg.
I had a sensation of floating, so I looked down at my feet.{p}

And there was my body, lying there.
Its face had gone pure white. It was nothing like the face of a living person.
(I see... I'm dead...)
Strangely, I was able to accept that fact without resisting.
..............................{p}

Before I knew it, I was standing in that restroom again.
One by one, they all went into the second stall from the back.
I went in too, as if I were being drawn inside.
(Ah, now I'm the one who'll become a school rumor...)
When I thought that, I strangely felt a sense of pride.
I realized that at some point, that mask had been fitted onto my face too.{p}
And then the restroom door closed...{p}

...I didn't lay a hand on the ones who drove me to my death.
Instead, I thought I'd be saved by driving their children to their deaths.
I felt that doing so would wash my ugly, twisted heart clean.
Is that cruel?
...Do you think I'm cruel?
Heh heh heh, think whatever you like.
...But remember this much.
When you commit a sin, you won't necessarily be the one who pays for it.
Through something you'd never expect, someone may be made to atone for the sin you committed.
And when that happens, it'll be too late for regrets.
But it doesn't matter anymore.
None of it...
I've achieved my goal, but I don't think I need to be saved anymore.
...I never thought that even in this state, a heart just like a human's would grow in me.
Just as those children came to enjoy bullying.
And just as it became a habit for them.
I've come to enjoy plunging people into the depths of terror.
Yes, you can find pleasure in anything at all.
It's a real problem, isn't it?
So I've decided to go on like this, chasing nothing but my own pleasure in this school.
Don't worry.
I won't do anything to you.
You're a good person.
I can tell...{p}

She turned her back to me.
Then she opened the window and gazed up at the eastern sky, where dawn was beginning to break.
What expression was she wearing behind her mask?
She put her hands to her mask once more.
This time, without hesitating, she slowly took it off.{p}

Then she gazed up at the sky again.
...If I could have lived in the same time as you, I'm sure we'd have been good friends...
I thought I heard her murmur that.
Then she slowly turned around to face me.{p}

"★"
Then dozens, hundreds of butterflies burst out of her face.
The butterflies flew around me, circling me on every side.
That many butterflies would normally seem creepy, but oh, how dreamlike it was...
They were blue butterflies, unlike any I had ever seen.
The butterflies danced in the morning sunlight.
Then, all at once, they flew out the window.{p}

I didn't know what to say.
But revenge was wrong.
I understood how she felt, too.
But they hadn't had anything to do with it directly, had they?
That was what I thought.
"Heh heh heh heh... I told you at the start, didn't I?
That I know what you're thinking.
Yes.
That's right.
They had nothing to do with it.
The ones to blame are their parents, not them.
But my revenge is over.
It's too late.
By killing their children, I'm giving them a taste of the grief my parents went through.{p}So, do you think this has saved me?"
I think you've been saved
There's no way you'll be saved

I see. Thank you.
You really do mean that.
...But you know, I already understand.
Doing this won't save me.
Revenge doesn't solve anything.
It only creates new people who can't be saved...
Even so, this was the only thing I could do.{p}

As she said that, she quietly looked back over her shoulder.
"Ah..."
Six new figures appeared behind her.
The people who had gathered for the newspaper club.
People who had been alive only a few hours ago.
People who now showed not the faintest pulse of life.
All of them had hollow eyes and were looking down at the floor.{p}

"Look, more new companions have been born.
Now I won't be lonely anymore...
But I suppose they must hate me.
And their hatred for me will twist my heart..."{p}
With that, she gently laid her hand on the mask.{p}"I'll ask you once more. Don't you want to see my face?"
I want to see it
I don't want to see it

I see. You really want to see it that badly?
...You might regret it, you know.{p}And you're fine with that...?
I won't regret it
I don't need to see it after all

I see.
You're braver than I thought.
Very well.
I'll show you... my heart.
She gently took off the mask.{p}

I didn't even have time to regret it.
It seemed I had died too.
The moment she took off her mask, a tremendous flood of emotion poured into me...
My heart hadn't been able to bear it.
That sorrow, that agony.
Is that how you end up feeling when you go on hating people for so long...?
But now, I feel as if I understand.
The heart of someone whose life was taken from them halfway through.{p}

She killed herself.
But the ones who killed her were the parents of those six.
She was murdered.
She was robbed of her life.
A hatred far beyond anything the living could ever imagine.
There must have been so much she still wanted to live for and do.
And she was robbed of it.
Maybe that bitter regret turns straight into hatred.
..............................{p}

I too had lost my life halfway through.
What about me?
Do I feel that bitter regret too?
And will I go on resenting someone too?
I don't understand my own heart.
Someday, I might become like her.
...And what about those six...?{p}

...I never laid a hand on the people who drove me to my death.
Instead, I'll be saved by driving their children to death.
I feel as if doing that will wash my ugly, twisted heart clean.
Is that cruel?{p}...Do you think I'm cruel?
That's not true!
You are cruel

"No. You're not cruel..."
For some reason, that was the answer I gave.
...Thank you.
Now I have nothing left to regret.
Whether I pass on from here or fall into hell, it doesn't matter anymore.
You don't seem to quite understand what I mean by being saved.
Being saved isn't about my soul.
Even though I died and am no longer of this world, my heart still remains.
It's that heart, my own heart, that will be saved.
Now, it's time...
I listened to her in silence.{p}

She turned back to face me.
And this time, without asking me, she took off the mask.{p}

Behind her mask....................
was a face so beautiful that words could never describe it.
Translucent white skin and pale pink cheeks.
And large, dark eyes that looked straight into mine...
Those eyes were so deep and clear that they showed no trace of doubt or worry.
The face looked at me and smiled.
I never once looked away from those eyes.{p}

Behind it lay a darkness, black and deep.
I felt as if I were about to be sucked into that darkness.{p}

The clatter of the mask hitting the floor brought me back to myself.
Even as her face changed, I had been able to watch it all without flinching.
She was neither a ghost nor a monster.
That was her heart...
When the mask fell to the floor and rocked, she was already gone.{p}

"You are cruel! That's no excuse for driving their children to their deaths! It's the lowest thing you could do!"
I shouted, furious.
...I see. So you say that kind of thing about me too.
No one understands my bitterness.
The only ones who grieved when I died were my father and mother.
I died with a powerful attachment to this world, and so here I am.
My heart given form, a being that can't truly exist...
But fine.
It's fine!
The six are already dead.
I'll be saved☆
She put her hand to the mask again.
This time, without hesitating, she took the mask off.{p}

Behind her mask....................
was a face so beautiful that words could never describe it.
Translucent white skin and pale pink cheeks.
And large, dark eyes that looked straight into mine...
Perhaps this was the face she had when she felt fulfilled.
I stood dumbstruck by her beauty.{p}

...At that moment.
A change came over her face.
Her beautiful face crumbled away like running wax.
Behind that melting face was another face.
That face had skin like a lizard's, dark and murky.
And big, round red eyes were staring at me.
"Still... not... saved...? Still... not... enough...?"
Her voice had changed into a low, muffled drone, like a stretched-out tape.
Only when she spoke did I see that a huge mouth split her face open from forehead to chin.
That mouth was lined with sharp fangs.
"You... too... will become... food... for my... salvation!"
With that, she lunged at me.{p}

The vertical mouth on her face split wide to the left and right and clamped down over my whole head.
Her fangs were buried deep in my head.
Hot blood ran down my face.
She doesn't know.
...She doesn't understand.
That no matter how much you hate someone, taking revenge accomplishes nothing.
It might calm her feelings, but there's no way it can save her.
Much less could she ever pass on by doing things like this.
And she will go on repeating the same thing for the sake of her own desires.
Never to be saved, for all eternity...
I die for the sake of her desire, a desire that can never be fulfilled.{p}

As she said that, she quietly looked back over her shoulder.
"Ah..."
Six new figures appeared behind her.
The people who had gathered for the newspaper club.
People who had been alive only a few hours ago.
People who now showed not the faintest pulse of life.
All of them had hollow eyes and were staring down at the floor.
"My new companions. Companions who will be with me forever, for all eternity.
I'm sure we won't have anything to talk about.
But you know, that's fine.
To me, they're a kind of proof that I took my revenge on their parents.
They can't defy me.
They're my faithful dolls.
I'll use them to gather more companions.
To start with... I'll have them make you one of my companions."
With that, she smoothly raised her right hand.
Sensing I was in danger, I bolted out of the restroom.{p}

"Whoa!"
Somehow, Shindo was standing outside the restroom.
I tried to shove him aside and get away.
I slammed into him with my shoulder as hard as I could.{p}

"☆"
I passed right through Shindo's body, and my momentum sent me sprawling.
I hurried to get up, but Shindo pinned me down.
The other five had surrounded me too.{p}

"Hey, {a}. You just don't know when to give up, huh?
That's not very manly.
Call it a samurai's mercy. I'll let you choose who kills you.
So, who's it gonna be?"
(Honestly, what an annoying question.
If I'm going to be killed, I just want whoever it is to do it in one go.)
I found myself thinking such stupid things.{p}"Come on, hurry up and choose..."
Akemi Iwashita
Nozomu Kazama
Shoji Arai
Makoto Shindo
Reiko Fukuzawa
Tomoharu Hosoda

Iwashita licked her lips with delight.
"All right, everyone, hold him down."
Shindo gave the order.
They all held me down firmly so that Iwashita could kill me more easily.{p}

"{a}, the time has finally come for me to kill you.
...If only I had been able to kill you back then, maybe I wouldn't have been possessed by an evil spirit..."
As she said it, Iwashita's face looked like an evil spirit itself.
Iwashita had to be truly possessed by an evil spirit.
"Now, are you ready?
I like you...
But only because you chose me... that is."{p}

Blood sprayed from my throat.
Iwashita's uniform was stained red.
But my eyes could no longer see color.
And then I couldn't even see light anymore.{p}

I see.
Of course...
There's nothing interesting about seeing my face.
But you do want to see it a little, don't you?
I can tell.
What you're thinking.
But I won't show it to you this time.
People often say one thing and think another, after all.
With that, she took her hand away from the mask.{p}
